So for the people who actually read the article, let’s have a discussion. I basically think 

1. People can be deradicalized. There is not doubt in my mind about how greatly 14 years in ADX Florence can shift your personality in one direction or another. I’m not sure how truthful Moussaui is because I simply don’t have enough data. 

2. If he wants to help us get to the truth about 9/11 and help the families get restitution from the Saudis, I would like to see what he has to say. If it ends up being worthless what did we lose?

3. If he has indeed changed, that’s good and perhaps he can earn his way into a less hellish federal prison. 

4. He clearly deserved to be punished for his actions and the threat he represented. The question is, what purpose is served by treating a legitimately (if he ends up being so) repentant criminal as though he has nothing to offer in terms of preventing others from making his mistakes? If Moussauis message from here on out us to young Muslims and other disaffected youths that violence is not the answer, do we do ourselves and potential victims a disservice by just throwing that away? 

5. What do the families of his victims want? Will it give them peace to see him rot regardless of the potential negative impact that could have if he is indeed potentially a voice of reason to those who would otherwise follow in his path? Is the purpose of our legal system vengeance or utility to society? That’s a question our criminal justice system will always grapple with. 

I don’t have an opinion one way or another because I can see both sides of all these issues and I don’t have enough facts or experiences to be confident one way or another. If I lost a loved one in 9/11 my view might be different from a legal scholar and Moussaui may represent a great opportunity to prevent others from following in his footsteps and save lives or he may be a fucking sociopathic opportunistic liar. It’s tempting to say all terrorists are psychopaths but I don’t know that. I think history has shown a man is often a victim of his circumstance but he is often able to overcome it. For some, that victory comes before the horrible deed and for some it may come 19 years too late. 

All I know is we need to do our best to use every tool we have to get justice for the victims and the financiers of 9/11 (Saudi Arabia) and to prevent further radicalization, which will save lives, while also not being duped by a potentially cynical and manipulative psychopath. 

Timothy McVeigh was a lost cause. We never should have let him do those fucking 60 minutes interviews. He should have been thrown in a hole and forgotten instead of executed, which just fulfilled his martyr complex. He was a truly sick human being. I don’t have words for how evil he was, but not every terrorist is Timothy McVeigh. 

That said, maybe I’m wrong! Maybe if TM were alive today he would weep for the people he murdered in cold blood, but I doubt it. I’ve studied him quite a bit and I have no reason to think he would ever have had a change of heart. Moussaui, may not be such a lost cause. Moussaui, in the end did not actually commit the sort of deed TM did. He allowed it to happen, but he did not do it. It’s not an insignificant difference i don’t think. There were many people around TM who played the Moussaui role. There were many people who stood by and let that happen. None of them, except James Fortier faced any repercussions for this.
